purpose: Progressive-disclosure manifest for one governed Freedom 250 research package.
title: International Organizations and U.S. Power Map — 2026
question: How do the major international organizations, treaty regimes, forums and parallel accords involving the United States actually work, and where can membership, money, standards, infrastructure or operating functions migrate without formal institutional replacement?
bluf: The reconciled 27-object map partly confirms modular international restructuring. The United States is selectively exiting some regimes, cutting funding or participation at some edges, refitting powerful incumbents from inside, incubating smaller coalitions and moving a few bounded functions into new bilateral or bespoke machinery. Bilateral global-health assistance is the strongest completed migration; the Board of Peace is the strongest new institutional setup; Artemis has shared non-binding machinery; Kyoto remains doctrine; no wholesale replacement of the old order is proved.
evidence_cutoff_note: All seven waves are reconciled through October 4, 2026. The October 5 Artemis principals meeting, PP-26, UNESCO's December 31 exit and UNFCCC's February 27, 2027 exit remained future. Forum direction, institutional decision, domestic implementation, funding, operation and outcome remain separate clocks.
use_note: The final reconciliation and 27-object registry control. Treat exit, defunding, parallel doctrine, shared machinery, resource migration and default use as separate states. Do not flatten the World Bank Group, treat a G7/G20 statement as an institutional act, treat a BIS-hosted or ITU technical standard as U.S. law, collapse IMO or WIPO membership into separately administered treaties, treat CERN observer status as membership, describe ITER requests as deliveries, or treat Board appointments, pledges and pre-deployment work as completed Gaza field governance.
